text: In Agello at 93122b647a, AppState is an @Observable @MainActor final class; its generation path calls engine.send(text:imageData:audioFileURL:) and passes the returned AsyncThrowingStream<ChatEvent, Error> to consume, which runs on the main actor, appends each chunk to a StreamAccumulator and writes the accumulated text into the reply's SwiftData ChatTurn only when at least 100 ms have passed since the last write (ContinuousClock), plus a final write after the stream ends.

In Agello at 93122b647a, LiteRTChatEngine is an actor; its nonisolated send(text:imageData:audioFileURL:) returns an AsyncThrowingStream whose build closure starts a Task running the actor-isolated runSend and sets onTermination to cancel that Task; runSend calls conversation.sendMessageStream(message, maxOutputTokens:) and, in a for-try-await loop that therefore runs isolated to the actor, yields for each LiteRTLM Message a ChatEvent.chunk whose ChatChunk carries chunk.toString as the text delta and chunk.channels["thought"] as the thought delta.

At LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544 (C API 1.0.0), litert_lm_conversation_send_message_stream parses message_json with nlohmann::json (InvalidArgument if it doesn't parse), builds OptionalArgs with CreateOptionalArgs, calls Conversation::SendMessageAsync with a callback made by CreateConversationCallback, and returns kLiteRtLmStatusOk as soon as SendMessageAsync returns OK, without waiting for the reply.

At LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544, Conversation::SendMessageAsync runs on the calling thread: it renders the turn's prompt text with GetSingleTurnText, appends the message(s) to history_ under history_mutex_, converts the text and messages to input data with model_data_processor_->ToInputDataVector, builds the internal callback with CreateInternalCallback, and calls session_->RunPrefillAsync with a callback that, when the prefill reports kDone (or failed only because the input was empty), saves the channel-content checkpoint if filter_channel_content_from_kv_cache is on and no channel is open, and then calls session_->RunDecodeAsync with the internal callback and the DecodeConfig.

At LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544, SessionAdvanced::RunPrefillAsync, after templating and tokenizing the contents, queues them with the execution manager's AddPrefillTask (dependent on last_task_ids_), and SessionAdvanced::RunDecodeAsync queues the decode with AddDecodeTask, passing the DecodeConfig's constraint, penalty, suppress-token, max-output-token and thinking settings.

At LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544, the task closure that ThreadedExecutionManager::AddPrefillTask creates runs, in order: StartTask, a cancel check, ResourceManager::AcquireExecutorWithContextHandler with the session's context handler, a second cancel check, ProcessAndCombineContents (encoding any image or audio), a third cancel check, Tasks::Prefill with wait_for_completion = true, recording last_prefill_token_id from the executor's processed tokens, releasing the executor and FinishTaskAndLogErrors; Tasks::Prefill returns InvalidArgument when the input has max_num_tokens tokens or more and otherwise calls executor.Prefill(inputs, params).

At LiteRT 362759838, LiteRtCompiledModelT::Run invokes the TFLite interpreter (interp_->Invoke() when the interpreter is used directly, otherwise the signature runner's Invoke()), mapping kTfLiteCancelled to kLiteRtStatusCancelled and other failures to 'Failed to invoke'; the ML Drift Metal delegate replaces its partition with a kernel whose TfLiteRegistration has custom_name 'LITERT_METAL' and invoke = Invoke, and that Invoke, inside @autoreleasepool, calls the DelegateKernelLiteRt steps (DequantizeInputs when quantized, BindExternalTensorBuffers, UploadIntermediateCpuTensorsToGpuMemory, HandleInputEvents, ConvertNonExternalInputTensorsToGpuMemory, then the run options, dispatch and output steps).

At LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544, the callback made by CreateInternalCallback, for each kProcessing Responses with text, appends Responses::GetTexts()[0] to a per-reply accumulated string and scans it from a cursor for channel and tool-call delimiters: text outside channels goes to the user callback as a Message built by model_data_processor.ToMessage from a copy of the released slice (SendMessage), channel text as {"role": "assistant", "channels": {name: text}} (SendMessageToChannel), and a tool-call block is held until its end delimiter; on kDone, or on kMaxNumTokensReached when return_error_on_max_tokens_reached is false, SendCompleteMessage sends the unflushed text, builds the complete message from the whole accumulated text, calls complete_message_callback and then calls the user callback with an empty Message.

In both the shipped Swift wrapper (85b1a776) and agello-next (7b872544), streamCallback handles a chunk's text by copying it into a Swift String (String(cString:)), converting it to Data and parsing it with JSONSerialization (appending any tool_calls to pendingToolCalls), and, when the object has content or channels, calling Conversation.jsonToMessage on the same string, which converts and parses it with JSONSerialization again before the Message is yielded to the stream's continuation.

In the documented build (agello-next, CPU sampler because no Metal sampler is linked), a plain Gemma 4 E4B decode step on the GPU writes 53,248 bytes of embeddings into the decode inputs (the token's 2,560-float embedding and 42 x 256-float per-layer embedding, FLOAT32) and the CPU sampler reads 524,288 bytes of FP16 logits (262,144 entries) back: 577,536 bytes per step, not counting the attention mask (one byte per allocated position), input_pos and param_tensor.

text: Our engine telemetry (agello/telemetry, agello-next 7b872544) defines five levels in agello_telemetry.h: 0 off; 1 counters and anomalies; 2 adds span aggregates (count, total, max, log2 histogram) and DynamicTracing signposts; 3 adds per-thread span ring buffers written as a Chrome/Perfetto trace; 4 adds diagnostic modes that change timing (per-kernel GPU timing, numerical probes); every probe first reads the level with one relaxed atomic load.

At agello-next 7b872544, agello_telemetry.h fixes the static span names (among them turn.prefill, turn.decode, template, tokenize, task.queue_wait, embedding_lookup, mask_fill, param_fill, run.prefill, run.decode, run.verify, run.drafter, decode.step, sample, logits_readback, detokenize, stream_callback, kv_clone, context_switch, host.lock_read, host.unlock_write and gpu.* run kinds), and Tasks::Decode wraps each call of the streamed callback in a stream_callback span and counts it in stream_chunks, so that span covers everything the callback does above Tasks for that chunk.

At LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544, //runtime/engine:litert_lm_main depends on :engine_impl_selected and //runtime/engine:litert_lm_advanced_main on :litert_lm_lib, which depends on :engine_impl_selected; :engine_impl_selected's only select branch is //runtime/core:engine_advanced_impl, which depends on //runtime/executor:default_static_gpu_accelerator; so, with that target selecting apple_static_gpu_accelerator for iOS and macOS unless litert_runtime_link_mode is dynamic (ours 43f0f5c3), a macOS build of either binary from our fork without the dynamic link mode links LiteRT's Metal accelerator statically. Not built or run.

At LiteRT-LM agello-next 7b872544, runtime/engine/litert_lm_main.cc reads only the flags --input_prompt, --input_prompt_file, --model_path, --backend (its own, default "gpu"), --visual_token_budget, --num_cpu_threads and --enable_ynnpack (besides overriding absl's minloglevel default), although it links :shared_flags, so the other shared flags are accepted and have no effect there; litert_lm_advanced_main reads the shared flags into its LiteRtLmSettings (for example --max_num_tokens, --benchmark, --async, --force_f32, --sampler_backend, --enable_speculative_decoding) and defines its own --backend with default "cpu".

tools/model-surgery/patch_rope.py (PowerBeef/agello-litert-lm branch agello, added in f2e7afa0; in neither pinned tree) patches the tf_lite_prefill_decode and tf_lite_mtp_drafter sections and writes a new .litertlm whose later sections move by 16 KiB-aligned deltas with the header's section offsets updated; its modes are '<in> <shift> <out>' (ADD of the shift to the float position after the rotary CAST), '<in> <shift> <out> --int' (the shift in INT32 before the CAST) and '<in> --split <out> [--block N]' (position = N*h + l with exact phases for positions 0..32767), where --block takes 512, 1024 or 2048 and defaults to 2048.

At the shipped commit 85b1a776, agello-bench's Package.swift builds against the LiteRT-LM package at LITERTLM_PACKAGE or, by default, '../..' (the fork checkout's root on the agello branch), whose Package.swift names Google's v0.18.0 release binaries CLiteRTLM (iOS) and CLiteRTLM_mac (macOS); so an agello-bench build without LITERTLM_PACKAGE on that branch measures Google's v0.18.0 macOS binary, and our runtime is measured by a separate build against the agello-next worktree.

agello-bench's usage text at 85b1a776 lists the run options --backend, --fp32, --kv, --mtp, --cache, --cold, --repeat, --warmup, --label, --out, --hash-model, --no-benchmark-mode, --telemetry N and --trace FILE (and --trace raises the telemetry level to at least 3), while the README's run-options sentence at 85b1a776 and at the agello tip 61c03d8e names --backend through --hash-model and --case but not --no-benchmark-mode, --telemetry or --trace.

text: Agello's scripts/device-harness.sh (93122b647a) passes the engine telemetry level to the app under test by exporting TEST_RUNNER_AGELLO_TELEMETRY set to $AGELLO_TELEMETRY, or 2 when that is unset.

litertlm_peek_main (LiteRT-LM python/litert_lm_builder) takes --litertlm_file (required) and --dump_files_dir (optional), and the PyPI wheel defined in the same BUILD declares the console scripts litert-lm-builder and litert-lm-peek.

//schema/model_info:model_info_cli takes the model path as its only argument, calls GetModelInfo and prints the ModelInfo report between separator lines; it prints a usage line and returns 1 without an argument, and prints the error and returns 1 when GetModelInfo fails.

tools/model-surgery/inspect_e4b.py (unchanged from 85b1a776 to the agello tip 61c03d8e) takes the model path and the options --section (default tf_lite_prefill_decode), --signature (default decode), --names and --layers, and its usage line runs it in the ~/.venvs/agello-tools venv.

At 85b1a776, BenchKit's Bench.load calls ExperimentalFlags.optIntoExperimentalAPIs(), sets ExperimentalFlags.enableBenchmark to the run's benchmarkMode (true unless --no-benchmark-mode), raises the engine telemetry level to 2 when benchmark mode is off and the level is below 2, and sets ExperimentalFlags.enableSpeculativeDecoding from --mtp.

BenchKit's EngineTelemetry (85b1a776) looks up the litert_lm_telemetry_* C functions with dlopen(nil)/dlsym at run time, so BenchKit runs against builds without them (Google's), where every telemetry call is a no-op.
At 85b1a776, agello-bench writes the engine load's telemetry snapshot to <out>.load-telemetry.json when --out is given and the load produced one.

agello-bench's compare.py (85b1a776) takes record files, --base LABEL (default: the first label seen) and --metrics (default prefillTPS decodeTPS ttft), leaves warm-up records out, and reports fidelity, identical replies against the base arm, per-case medians and IQRs, each arm's change with a 95% bootstrap interval, and a noise band from the base arm's even against odd repetitions.

agello-bench's telemetry.py (85b1a776) reads agello-bench JSONL records (with --label, --case and --weights-gb), an Agello harness report, a .load-telemetry.json snapshot, or with --graph DIR a folder of GPU graphs written with AGELLO_TELEMETRY_GRAPH_DIR.
